=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Draft against Buyer Playbook

**Status:** Working analysis for the deal team, not a sign-off. Nothing in the Seller package is accepted. Its "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "agreed at principal level", "market standard" and "pre-cleared" labels are the Seller's assertions. Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3 they do not bind us, and no buyer clearance appears in our record. Several Seller numbers also match fallbacks, but a fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. The "[OPEN]" tag is not used anywhere in the package, so I have treated every clause as open.

---

## 1. Departures from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture (Clauses 12.1 to 12.3, 13)

| Term | Seller draft | Buyer playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranty cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (20% is a fallback needing Frost's written authority; none given) | AUD 1.2m below opening position |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; small claims excluded |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price) | AUD 50,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket mechanic | Excess only (deductible) | Seller liable from first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of claims |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 months needs Frost's written approval; none given) | 6 months shorter |
| Application of time limits | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Would pull Title and Fundamental claims into the general regime |

**Reasoning:** Taken together, the Seller's terms would leave the Buyer with very little general warranty recourse. The AUD 250,000 deductible alone, combined with the AUD 25,000 de minimis, could defeat claims across the diligence areas on which we are already seeing issues (Bluefen, Ironquay, Sandbar, bonuses). The "10 to 20% cap / about 1% basket / 12 to 18 months" market-context paragraph is the Seller's characterisation. It is not a basis for accepting our fallbacks, and the playbook does not adopt it.

### B. Fundamental / Title claims

The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

**Departure:** The playbook requires a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. The Seller proposal removes all four protections. **Reject outright.** Title and capacity are the core of what the Buyer is paying for, so an "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify this.

### C. Carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct

The package contains **no fraud carve-out**. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."

**Departure:** The playbook carves fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this. **Reject.** Insert the carve-out expressly. Note that no authority may waive it, so this is not a point for the Frost fallback process.

### D. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paragraphs 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 11)

- **DL 1.1** discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the entire data room (including DD-002 to DD-012) as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026.
- **DL 1.2** discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records.
- **Schedule 7** relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers.

**Departure:** The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. These paragraphs would effectively disclose everything against the warranties, which makes the warranty package close to meaningless. **Reject.** DL 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable in principle, but DL 11 ("the Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement") should be read as having no effect on Buyer rights.

### E. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

The Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Departure:** The playbook deletes blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and may never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. **Reject.** Clause 8.3 as drafted is the most dangerous provision in the package, because it would convert data-room diligence findings into a Buyer waiver.

### F. Bluefen consent (Clause 3 / 6.3; DL 2)

- The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat the consent as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent.
- DL 2 confirms that **no final written Bluefen consent** and **no evidence of satisfied conditions** have been provided.
- The customer represents about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%).

**Departure:** The playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. **Reject.** Bluefen is the highest-value commercial issue in the package.

### G. Riverlark facility (Clause 2 / 7; DL 3)

- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The release is to be provided **after** Completion.
- DL 3 confirms the facility **has not been repaid** and no final discharge of security is included.

**Departure:** The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. **Reject.** The payout should appear in the funds flow.

### H. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL 5; DD-005)

- AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the draft funds flow and described as "a matter for the Seller."
- DL 5 says the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

**Departure:** The playbook requires the amount to be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude it. **Reject.** Push for seller funding of the bonuses **and** their triggered on-costs, which are currently unquantified. Also clarify who bears the cost if continued-employment conditions are not met.

### I. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL 4; DD-004/DD-010)

- The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate."
- DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, which is not independent bank verification. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Departure:** The playbook requires broadening the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. **Reject.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction, so it must be independently checked (bank records or Ironquay confirmation) rather than assumed correct.

### J. Export / privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL 6; DD-006)

- The Seller calls the matter "preliminary" and "not expected to be material."
- DL 6 records an export of about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. It does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.

**Playbook position:** Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates.

**Assessment:** The Seller's "not material" characterisation is not supported by the record, and we should not adopt it. Equally, we should not assert a breach. The correct stance is to require:
- preservation of access and delivery logs;
- a defined investigation scope and timetable;
- written updates before Completion;
- a Seller warranty about known facts.

Whether a specific indemnity is needed is a decision for Amelia Frost. The playbook does not prescribe one. Privacy counsel should assess the Privacy Act (Cth) position in parallel, without treating the matter as a breach in our communications.

### K. Sandbar renewals (Clause 8 disclosure; DL 8; DD-008/DD-011)

- The Seller describes three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 total) as "ordinary-course operating costs."
- DL 8 says the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Playbook position:** Assess the renewals. Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct from price.

**Pushback:** Reject the "ordinary course" characterisation until we have the contracts, termination rights, timing and whether any amounts have accrued. Confirm the tie-in between the renewals and the 2026 price mechanics, but do not accept a price deduction or Debt classification on the current record.

### L. Tax and IP (Seller's Update)

The Seller says the tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."

**Departure:** The playbook keeps Tax and IP terms **open**, assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution, and requires separate categories. **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** These categories must not be pulled into the general regime.

### M. Title (Seller's Update; DL 10; DD-012)

The Seller says title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."

**Departure:** The playbook treats DD-012 as an internal, supplied source, not independent proof. We need independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. **Reject** reliance on DD-012 alone. Required evidence includes:
- an ASIC company extract and current share register search;
- a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares;
- board and shareholder authority for the sale;
- confirmation that no third-party consents or pre-emptive rights are triggered.

### N. Items outside the playbook (flag for diligence)

- **Office lease (DD-007; DL 7):** A notification obligation is identified, but the material does not state whether landlord consent to the share sale is needed. Confirm with the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009; DL 9):** An assignment restriction exists. Confirm whether a change of control is caught.

These are not addressed in the playbook. They should be confirmed as diligence items and reported to Amelia Frost, but I would not make recommendations on them beyond confirmation.

---

## 2. Recommendations

**Priority 1: Commercial risk items (require resolution before Completion)**
1. **Bluefen:** Require effective written consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
2. **Riverlark:** Include a current payout figure in the funds flow and repay directly from Completion funds. Reject post-completion release unless an irrevocable undertaking is given and Amelia Frost approves.
3. **Employee bonuses:** Add AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific line item, or make them seller-funded.

**Priority 2: Structural protections (non-negotiable)**
4. **Fraud carve-out:** Insert a carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all limitations. No waiver.
5. **Fundamental / Title regime:** Restore the separate regime (100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar). Reject the Seller's "administrative simplicity" merger.
6. **Disclosure:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and Schedule 7 general disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure only.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete Clause 8.3's blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and may never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Separate categories:** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims in separate regimes. Reject the "settled under the general regime" language.

**Priority 3: Warranty economics (counter at opening positions)**
9. **General cap:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20% without Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
10. **De minimis and basket:** Counter at AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
11. **Claims period:** Counter at 24 months. Do not offer 18 months without Frost's written approval.

**Priority 4: Specific items requiring evidence**
12. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and independently verify the AUD 180,000 (bank records or Ironquay confirmation).
13. **Export/privacy incident (DD-006):** Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope, written updates before Completion, and a Seller warranty on known facts. Do not characterise the matter as a breach or as immaterial. Frost to decide on any specific indemnity. Privacy counsel to review in parallel.
14. **Sandbar renewals:** Obtain contracts, termination rights, timing and accrual position. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction on the current record.
15. **Title:** Obtain independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR search, share register search, authority resolutions). Do not rely on DD-012 alone.
16. **Tax and IP:** Keep open. Reject the "settled" characterisation.

**Process actions**
- Send Amelia Frost a summary of Priorities 1 and 2 for immediate decision. Any fallback proposal needs her written authority identifying the specific draft.
- Respond to the Seller that the "[STANDARD]" labels, "FINAL" marking and "pre-cleared" status are not accepted, and that the package remains under full review.
- Confirm the lease (landlord consent) and Mossvale (assignment) positions as diligence items.

---

*This analysis is based only on the Seller's package and the playbook summary provided. It has not been checked against the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), the full draft SPA, or NSW and Commonwealth law. It should be reviewed by responsible counsel before any position is communicated to the Seller.*
